name: Canada
summary: Canada's main stock exchange, the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX), traces its roots to 1852 and is part of TMX Group. Toronto pioneered computer-assisted trading (1977) and launched the world's first ETF (1990). Canada moved to next-day (T+1) settlement on 27 May 2024, one day before the US.

currency.name: Canadian dollar
currency.note: Canadian shares are priced in Canadian dollars, so a euro investor carries currency risk: moves of the Canadian dollar against the euro change the value of holdings in euros (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX, part of TMX Group)
exchanges.founded: 1852 (Association of Brokers formed on 24 October 1852); formally created in 1861
exchanges.hours: Opening at 09:30 ET, continuous trading until 16:00 with the Market on Close facility from 15:50, and an extended session 16:15–17:00 at the last sale price only.
exchanges.note: TSX Venture Exchange is TMX's market for early-stage companies. Toronto uses the same daylight saving rules as New York.

indexes.name: S&P/TSX Composite Index
indexes.description: Canada's broad benchmark for Toronto-listed shares. Launched in 1977 as the TSE 300 Composite Index; S&P Dow Jones Indices took over its management in 2002 and it was renamed.

regulators.name: Provincial securities commissions (for example the Ontario Securities Commission)
regulators.role: Securities regulation in Canada is provincial; the commissions coordinate through the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA).

regulators.name: Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO)
regulators.role: National self-regulatory organisation for investment dealers and mutual fund dealers, and for trading on Canadian marketplaces.

investorProtection.name: Canadian Investor Protection Fund (CIPF)
investorProtection.text: If a CIRO member firm becomes insolvent, CIPF generally protects an individual's property up to C$1 million for all general accounts combined, plus C$1 million each for retirement accounts and education savings plans.

investorProtection.name: Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC)
investorProtection.text: Eligible deposits at member institutions are insured up to C$100,000 per insured category, principal and interest included.

settlement.csd: CDS Clearing and Depository Services (part of TMX Group)
settlement.note: Canada switched one day before the US (28 May 2024) because of a US holiday.

source.title: Canadian securities regulators announce move to T+1 settlement cycle, 27 May 2024 (CSA)

rules.title: Regulation is provincial
rules.text: Canada has no single national securities regulator: each province and territory has its own, coordinated through the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA). Dealers are overseen by the self-regulatory organisation CIRO.

taxes.glance: Non-residents: 25% Canadian tax on dividends (Part XIII), reducible under a tax treaty, usually by giving the payer form NR301. Gains on listed shares are generally not taxed in Canada for non-residents unless they are 'taxable Canadian property' (holdings of 25% or more in property-rich companies).

items.title: Dividends for non-residents
items.text: Non-residents pay 25% tax on dividends and other amounts taxable under Part XIII. A tax treaty can lower the rate; the payer usually needs form NR301 (declaration of eligibility for treaty benefits) to apply it.

items.title: Capital gains for non-residents
items.text: Non-residents are taxed in Canada on gains from 'taxable Canadian property'. Listed shares count only if, in the previous 60 months, the investor (with related persons) held 25% or more of a class and more than 50% of the share value came from Canadian real estate or resources.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q); any higher Canadian tax must be reduced under the treaty or reclaimed in Canada.

sources.title: NR4: Non-resident tax withholding, remitting and reporting (Canada Revenue Agency)
NR301: Declaration of eligibility for benefits under a tax treaty (Canada Revenue Agency)
Disposing of or acquiring certain Canadian property (Canada Revenue Agency)

access: Many Austrian banks and brokers offer trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange; check costs for converting euros into Canadian dollars.
Some large Canadian companies are also listed in the US and can be bought there in US dollars.
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on Canadian, North American or developed-market indexes (Category H).

history.text: Toronto businessmen form an 'Association of Brokers' on 24 October, the framework for the Toronto Stock Exchange.
The association formally creates the Toronto Stock Exchange; trading is limited to daily half-hour sessions in 18 securities.
Toronto launches the world's first Computer Assisted Trading System (CATS) and the TSE 300 Composite Index.
The world's first ETF, the Toronto 35 Index Participation Fund, is created.
Toronto becomes the first exchange in North America to introduce decimal trading, and the largest in North America to close its trading floor and go fully electronic.
Canada moves to T+1 settlement on 27 May.

funFacts: In its early years, the Toronto Stock Exchange saw only two or three trades a day.
When World War I broke out, the Toronto Stock Exchange closed for three months out of fear of a financial panic.
